calls.head: The Senators should drive the play
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Senators have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Flyers one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Senators’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia only a 38% chance, and they proved us wrong.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 62% chance, but Philadelphia had other ideas.

surprises.head: Philadelphia couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Philadelphia usually gets worse looks than most teams, and Ottawa usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Philadelphia’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 2.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.1% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 350 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: At last, a first win for the Flyers
paras: The Flyers won for the first time this season, at the tenth try, after starting 0-6-3. Drake Batherson got the scoring started for the Senators early in the second, and that was all they would get. Porter Martone tied it 1-1 for Philadelphia just over three minutes later, and Matvei Michkov put the Flyers ahead for good on the power play late in the period. The Sens’ Thomas Chabot left later in the period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was ruled out for 1-2 weeks with an upper-body injury. Trevor Zegras added the empty-netter with 14 seconds left to make it 3-1.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Dan Vladař made 25 saves for the Flyers, and Linus Ullmark stopped 25 of 27 at the other end. It was Ullmark’s first loss of the season, after six straight wins to open it. The Flyers improved to 1-6-3, still last in the Metropolitan, while the Senators dropped to 6-3-0, slipping to third in the Atlantic.
